extracted.intended_audience: State and Federally Facilitated Exchanges, health insurance issuers, agents/brokers, and other stakeholders commenting on or implementing individual market Exchange program integrity and payment-rule proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble and proposed regulatory amendments for Exchange program integrity, enrollment periods, special enrollment periods, actuarial value rules, premium adjustment methodology, and related issuer and Exchange operational standards for the individual market (proposed effective years starting PY2026).

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic reenrollment hierarchy (§155.335(j)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Current rule at §155.335(j)(4) allows Exchanges to move a CSR-eligible enrollee from a bronze QHP and re-enroll them into a silver QHP for an upcoming plan year if a silver QHP is available in the same product, with the same provider network, and with a lower or equivalent net premium after the application of APTC as the bronze plan into which the enrollee would otherwise have been re-enrolled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal: remove §155.335(j)(4). Rationale: consumer awareness problem the policy originally aimed to address is substantially less today; the automatic movement may confuse consumers, undermine consumer choice, and create unexpected tax liability. Historical context provided of prior hierarchy changes and solicitation of comments on revising re-enrollment hierarchy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premium payment threshold limitation (§155.400(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuers may implement a premium payment threshold policy determining when partial premium payment is sufficient to avoid consequences for non-payment of premiums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal: remove paragraphs (2) and (3) of §155.400(g) to eliminate issuer options to implement a fixed dollar and/or gross percentage-based premium payment threshold; limit issuers to net percentage-based premium payment threshold at §155.400(g)(1). Rationale: ensure enrollees do not remain enrolled without paying at least some premium, since fixed dollar or gross percentage thresholds could allow extended enrollment after only binder payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Enrollment Period (OEP) dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual OEP for coverage through individual market Exchanges (and non-grandfathered individual coverage outside an Exchange) determines the window during which people may enroll for coverage for the upcoming benefit year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal: for benefit years starting January 1, 2026 and beyond, change OEP from November 1 through January 15 to November 1 through December 15 of the calendar year preceding the benefit year. Rationale: reduce adverse selection and encourage continuous coverage; would also apply outside Exchanges for non-grandfathered coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal monthly SEP for APTC-eligible enrollees ≤150% FPL (§155.420(d)(16))
rubrics_metrics.description: A monthly special enrollment period currently exists for qualified individuals/enrollees (or their dependents) who are eligible for APTC and whose projected household income is at or below 150 percent of the FPL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal: remove §155.420(d)(16) and make conforming changes to repeal this monthly SEP. Rationale: improve the risk pool by reducing adverse selection (people enrolling only when they need care), encourage continuous coverage, and lower premiums. Historical notes: this SEP was temporary and has been modified/removed/extended in prior notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-enrollment verification of SEP eligibility (§155.420(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification of applicants' eligibility for all categories of individual market special enrollment periods (SEPs) prior to enrollment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal: enable HHS to reinstate pre-enrollment verification for all SEP categories and require all Exchanges to conduct pre-enrollment verification for at least 75% of new enrollments through SEPs. Exchanges likely could meet requirement by verifying their two most used SEPs. Rationale: response to evidence of misuse/abuse of SEPs to gain coverage outside OEP; protect program integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on providing sex-trait modification as an EHB (§156.115(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an issuer may include sex-trait modification services as an essential health benefit (EHB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal: amend §156.115(d) so that an issuer of coverage subject to EHB requirements may not provide sex-trait modification as an EHB beginning with Plan Year 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premium adjustment percentage methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodology for estimating premium growth (premium adjustment percentage) used to set a rate of increase for parameters like maximum annual limitation on cost sharing, required contribution percentage (MEC affordability), and employer shared responsibility payment amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal: update methodology to comprehensively reflect premium growth across affected markets by re-adopting the premium growth measure used for PY2020 and PY2021, and apply it starting PY2026 to related parameters (including PY2026 maximum annual limitation on cost sharing and required contribution percentage under §155.605(d)(2)). Background: describes prior methodologies using NHEA ESI premium measures and history of methodological changes and guidance practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: De minimis actuarial value (AV) thresholds for EHB plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowable AV variation (de minimis range) for plans subject to EHB requirements when determining level of coverage (bronze, silver, gold, platinum) to account for actuarial estimate differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal: beginning PY2026, change de minimis thresholds for AV to +2/−4 percentage points for all individual and small group market plans subject to AV requirements under EHB package, except expanded bronze plans where de minimis would be +5/−4. Also propose wider de minimis thresholds for income-based CSR plan variations. Rationale: adjust flexibility around AV calculations for plan certification and silver variation calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: EHB statutory requirements and non-discrimination standards (ACA §1302)
rubrics_metrics.description: EHB package must be equal in scope to benefits under a typical employer plan and include at least 10 specified categories; Secretary must define EHB to reflect balance and not be designed to discriminate based on age, disability, or expected length of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists 10 categories (ambulatory patient services; emergency services; hospitalization; maternity and newborn care; mental health and substance use disorder services; prescription drugs; rehabilitative and habilitative services and devices; laboratory services; preventive and wellness services and chronic disease management; pediatric services including oral and vision). Secretary guidance must ensure balance among categories, account for diverse population health needs, and prohibit denials of EHBs based on age, life expectancy, disability, medical dependency, or quality of life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Open Enrollment Period requirement (ACA §1311(c)(6)(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: Secretary must require an Exchange to provide for annual OEPs after the initial enrollment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides statutory basis for setting OEP dates and for making conforming regulatory changes to OEP windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to require Special Enrollment Periods (ACA §1311(c)(6)(C) and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Secretary may require Exchanges to provide SEPs specified in section 9801 of the Code and other SEPs under analogous circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory basis for the Exchange SEP framework; used to justify regulatory SEP types, lengths, and triggers referenced throughout the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: QHP certification criteria and sufficient choice of providers (ACA §1311(c) & §1311(c)(1)(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for certification of Qualified Health Plans (QHPs), including ensuring a sufficient choice of providers and that offering a plan through the Exchange is in the interests of qualified individuals and employers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary's regulations set certification criteria; Exchanges certify plans based on these criteria and may consider network, product availability, and consumer interests. Historical context: Exchange certification authority described and referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent and broker enrollment and assistance procedures (ACA §1312(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures under which a State may allow agents or brokers to enroll qualified individuals and employers in QHPs and assist in applying for APTC and CSRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides statutory authority and background for subsequent program integrity rules and documentation/consent requirements for agents/brokers and web-brokers discussed in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawful presence requirement for enrollment and subsidies (ACA §§1312(f)(3), 1401, 1402(e), 1412(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals must be citizens, nationals, or lawfully present in the U.S. to enroll in a QHP through an Exchange and to be eligible for PTC, APTC, and CSRs; Federal payments are not allowed for those not lawfully present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background on rulemaking and DACA definition changes (including May 8, 2024 DACA Rule reinterpreting 'lawfully present' to include DACA recipients for certain benefits). Provides statutory citation and enforcement context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange oversight, financial integrity, and fraud prevention authority (ACA §§1313, 1321, 1321(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Secretary has authority to oversee financial integrity of State Exchanges, compliance with HHS standards, efficient and non-discriminatory administration, and to implement measures to reduce fraud and abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains HHS authority to issue regulations and standards for establishment and operation of Exchanges; provides context for program integrity proposals throughout the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined enrollment and participation in data matching (§1413)
rubrics_metrics.description: Secretary directed to establish, subject to minimum requirements, streamlined enrollment for QHPs and insurance affordability programs and require Exchanges to participate in third-party data matching for eligibility determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background and statutory mandate supporting verification, redetermination, and data-matching processes described later (income verification, IRS/SSA data use).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to file taxes and reconcile APTC — Exchange notification and discontinuation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchanges determine APTC ineligibility if tax filers who received APTC fail to file tax returns and reconcile APTC as required; rules specify notice and discontinuation timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical/finalized policies: Exchanges cannot determine ineligibility for APTC for failure to file unless they send direct notification (2018 Payment Notice), later removed; 2024 Payment Notice required waiting until two consecutive years of failure to reconcile before discontinuing APTC, and 2025/2026 Notices added or clarified notice requirements for first and second years of non-reconciliation. Rationale: balance program integrity with notification and due process; procedural timeline changes described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income inconsistency and alternative verification process (§155.320(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a tax filer's attested projected annual household income differs from IRS/SSA/current income sources (income inconsistency), Exchanges must follow alternative verification processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originally required Exchange to notify applicant of inconsistency and require documentary evidence within 90 days. Court vacatur led to rescission of some revisions; later revisions (2024 Payment Notice) require Exchanges to accept self-attestation when IRS call completed but tax return data unavailable, and require an automatic 60-day extension in addition to the 90 days for resolving inconsistencies. Background includes legal developments (City of Columbus v. Cochran).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual eligibility redetermination and renewal standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for Exchanges to conduct annual eligibility redeterminations and renewals of coverage, including methods for redetermination and notice content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical rules allowed Exchanges to choose from one of three methods for annual redeterminations; prior solicitations sought comment on whether redetermination notices should describe how cost-sharing would change. Proposed considerations include modifying automatic re-enrollment (e.g., re-enroll without APTC when APTC would cover entire premium) and other re-enrollment process changes to address program integrity concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution of initial premium payment to past-due premiums for new coverage (§147.104(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an issuer may attribute payment of premium for new coverage to past-due premiums from prior coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal: remove §147.104(i) that restricts issuers from attributing payment for new coverage to past-due premiums. New proposal would allow issuers to attribute initial premium paid to effectuate new coverage to amounts owed from prior coverage (without the prior 12-month limit from Market Stabilization Rule). States may still impose limitations. Rationale: allow issuers to collect owed amounts consistent with their premium payment policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conforming amendment to limited OEP triggers (§147.104(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory cross-reference that currently excludes §155.420(d)(16) as a triggering event for a limited OEP for coverage offered outside an Exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal: remove §147.104(b)(2)(i)(G) to reflect removal of the monthly SEP at §155.420(d)(16). Clarifies that the intent is not to add §155.420(d)(16) as a trigger for limited OEP outside Exchanges but to reflect repeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEP parameters, effective dates, and verification history
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards governing SEP effective dates, availability/length, types, and verification practices across Exchanges and for coverage outside Exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background summary of SEP rulemaking history, including changes to effective dates, coverage effective date rules for births/adoptions, inclusion of release-from-incarceration, assessments to detect SEP abuse (consumer documentation collection), pre-enrollment verification initiatives beginning 2017, and numerous Payment Notice changes (2020, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025). Use this for context when implementing or evaluating SEP policies and verification procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actuarial justification factors for plan-specific rate variation (§156.80(d)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan-specific actuarially justified factors an issuer may use to vary premium rates for a plan from its market-wide index rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 2026 Payment Notice revision: require actuarially justified plan-specific factors to include the AV and cost-sharing design of the plan, and where permitted by State authority, to account for CSR amounts provided to eligible enrollees under §156.410 (provided issuer does not otherwise receive reimbursement). This guides allowable rate differentiation and actuarial documentation.
